title: Model scout workflow automation + credit-weighted sampling pilot
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Our current model scouting and field-sampling process is manual, ad-hoc, and expensive to run at scale. We rely on periodic hand-curated probes and uniform sampling across customer workloads which underweights heavy-call customers and misses early signals from high-risk verticals.

Objective: Build a small, repeatable pilot that automates end-to-end model scouting (signal capture -> enrichment -> ranking) and introduces a credit-weighted sampling strategy so high-volume or high-SLA customers have proportionally more representation in model-behavior probes. The pilot should surface substitution risk, performance regressions, and procurement-relevant signals with minimal manual intervention.

Scope:
- End-to-end pipeline orchestration for selected geos (NA/EU) and workload cohorts (embeddings, short-gen, RAG).
- Credit-weighted sampling engine that consumes usage telemetry and customer tiers to produce prioritized probe lists.
- Dashboard with top-20 substitution risk signals and a small alerting surface for P1 regressions.
- Integration points: telemetry (internal infra metrics), product analytics (Amplitude), and model eval harness (internal repo).

Out of scope: full enterprise rollout, private deployment instrumentation (will be follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: Automated pipeline produces daily prioritized probe lists for at least two workload cohorts
Credit-weighted sampler uses usage + SLA tier to adjust sampling weights and is configurable via config file
Dashboard displays provenance for each signal, last-run timestamp, and confidence score
Pilot generates at least one actionable substitution or regression alert during pilot window
Runbook documented with rollback and privacy checks for customer-sample selection
comments: 2026-02-22: Kickoff with Data-Infra and Analytics. Agreed on initial cohorts: embeddings (short vectors) and short-text generation (<256 tokens). Action: analytics to provide customer usage snapshot by 2026-02-26. — Asha
2026-02-27: Analytics delivered usage snapshot. Notable: ~12 customers account for 62% of embedding units in NA. Decided to weight top decile x5. — Liam

2026-03-03: Design review: privacy team flagged potential PII in sample payloads. Added automated scrub step to pipeline and requirement to run scrubbed payloads through compliance check. — Privacy (R. Gomez)
2026-03-06: Engineering PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/model-scout/pulls/48. Initial DAG + credit sampler implemented. Needs unit tests and e2e smoke test. — Eng (M. Chen)
2026-03-09: PM review: Confirmed metrics. Success metrics: signal precision >= 0.6 and mean time to first actionable <= 7 days for pilot. If both met, expand to dedicated cohort. — Asha
2026-03-10: Deployed to staging. Ran first daily job. Dashboard populated with 14 signals (mostly latency skew on quantized variants). Next: runbook writeup and stakeholder demo 2026-03-17. — Liam
risks: Privacy: sampling could accidentally surface customer data if scrub step misses edge-cases
Signal quality: credit-weighting might overfit to a few customers and miss broader regressions
Ops cost: automated probes increase load on hosted endpoints and could affect SLAs if not throttled
mitigations: Implement conservative scrub + hashed identifiers for sample traces before storage
Run parallel uniform-sampling baseline during pilot to measure drift vs weighted approach
Apply rate limits and traffic caps; coordinate with capacity planning for pilot window
notes: This ticket intentionally limits scope to NA/EU and two cohorts to keep iteration fast. If pilot success criteria met, schedule expansion planning into cycle 2026-W13. Consider mapping this engine to procurement trigger thresholds in later phase.
